newsitem.title: USA: IPAA says U.S. oil production decline to reverse.
newsitem.headline: IPAA says U.S. oil production decline to reverse.

text.p: The Independent Producers Association of America (IPAA) on Wednesday forecast that domestic U.S. crude oil production would reverse its decline in 1997 for the first time in 12 years.
IPAA forecast domestic production would increase this year by 0.3 percent to 6.49 million barrels per day (bpd), the first increase since 1985.
IPAA is a trade body representing indpendent U.S. oil exploration and production companies.
"Prices coupled with technology gains and offshore activity are the main reason for the increase," IPAA said in a presentation at an investment symposium in New York for independent producers.

Large oil and gas finds, such as the giant Mars field in deepwater Gulf of Mexico, account for some of the production gains but increases from marginal wells -- categorized as those producing 15 bpd or less, which account for 40 percent of domestic output -- are also a factor in the turnaround.

Nevertheless, oil imports and the U.S. dependence on foreign oil as a percentage of its consumption will continue to increase and the decline in domestic production will reappear in the new century, the IPAA predicted.
Oil imports will reach 9.7 million bpd this year, up 2.9 percent on last year and accounting for 53% of total U.S. petroleum demand.
U.S. production will increase to 6.58 million bpd by 2000 but decline thereafter at a rate of about 0.6 percent a year, reaching 6.2 million bpd in 2010.
Imports will rise to 10.7 million bpd by 2000, or 55 percent of demand, and to 13.4 million bpd by 2010, 62 percent of demand, compared with 8.8 million bpd in 1995.
